key_findings: PTP1B localizes to inhibitory postsynapses of spinal SOM+ interneurons and directly binds GlyR alpha1 via its intracellular large loop, dephosphorylating Tyr339.
PTP1B negatively regulates glycinergic transmission; knockdown increases GlyR-mIPSC amplitudes.

CFA inflammation (and SNI) upregulates spinal PTP1B, causing glycinergic disinhibition, SOM+ interneuron hyperexcitability and mechanical (static and dynamic) allodynia; PTP1B knockdown or inhibitor XXII alleviates these.
PTP1B and GPR39 compete for GlyR alpha1 binding; GPR39 activation restores glycinergic inhibition.
